comment: The monitoring framework under-measures whether a shared platform becomes institutionalised and used. HISP has assessed country maturity of DHIS2 as an MIS platform across health and non-health domains. Relevant RHIS/DHIS2 measures include coexistence/triangulation of aggregate, event and Tracker data; end users have access to analytic dashboards; active use at subnational level; API integrations; local configuration/support capability; upgrade sustainability; and retirement of duplicative reporting systems.

public.text: The monitoring framework under-measures whether a shared platform becomes institutionalised and used. HISP has assessed country maturity of DHIS2 as an MIS platform across health and non-health domains. Relevant RHIS/DHIS2 measures include coexistence/triangulation of aggregate, event and Tracker data; end users have access to analytic dashboards; active use at subnational level; API integrations; local configuration/support capability; upgrade sustainability; and retirement of duplicative reporting systems.
public.suggestedRevision: We recommend measures for "routine system use" to catpure DPI-H institutionalization. Are data review meetings routine? How frequently are outages reported for civil registry systems? Are all facility and clients registered across the country -- and if not, does it prevent use of the system? Are data exchanged from other systems visible to healthcare providers, or do they inform critical M&E indicators? Have previous reporting systems been retired, or are they still add-on? See for example PRISM Framework https://www.measureevaluation.org/resources/prism.html
